messages:
sre_oncall: :rotating_light: Support escalation — multiple EU customers reporting p99 TLS handshake latency spikes starting ~07:10 UTC. Support tickets #2345, #2347, #2350. Affects hosted API endpoints in eu-west-1. Observed p99 ~1.6s (baseline ~120ms). Any immediate triage?
network_eng: Looking. Do we have flow logs/traceroutes from affected POPs?
support_engineer: I have a few customer pcaps and curl timings. Example: `curl -v --tlsv1.3 https://api.redwood.ai/health -w "%{time_connect}s %{time_appconnect}s" -o /dev/null` -> shows `0.12 1.58`. They see multiple SYN retransmits before TLS completes.
infra_lead: Can you paste the flow logs? Also check if there was any routing rollout or edge config pushed around 07:00-07:15.
support_engineer: Snippet from one pcap: `Client -> SYN -> SYN/ACK, client ACK -> Client TLS ClientHello (SNI api.redwood.ai) -> Server TLS Alert: unexpected_message -> Server resets TLS` then client retries, next handshake completes but ~1.5s later. Looks like server sent alert on first ClientHello.
network_eng: That smells like SNI mismatch / virtual host routing hitting backend that doesn't like the SNI. Checking LB logs now.
prod_reliability: We deployed an updated cert rotation agent to eu-west-1 at 06:50 UTC but it should be no-op. Rolling back? :eyes:
infra_lead: Wait - cert agent touched SNI routing table? Not supposed to. Assigning to @network_eng and @infra_lead to correlate.
network_eng: From edge LB access logs: a subset of connections from APIGW-POOL-7 were routed to backend pool B which had a config mismatch (missing `server_name` mapping). That backend returns TLS alert 40 on first handshake. After retry it hits proper backend. Need to confirm why affinity broke.
dns-bot: DNS health checks: no large query spikes. Geo-DNS served eu-west-1 as expected. No TTL changes.
network_eng: Looking at BGP logs — there was a transient route flap from peering partner peer-12 at 07:09:33 that caused ~30s of path shifts for ~2% of traffic. That could explain subset of client sessions being diverted to older backend pool.
support_engineer: Customers on same ISP saw correlated timestamps, matches the BGP flap windows.
infra_lead: Mitigation options: 1) Remove peer-12 routes (depref) 2) Reweight BGP to prefer internal transit for eu-west 3) Hotfix backend pool B config (add server_name mapping) 4) Pause cert-agent rollout until validated.
prod_reliability: I pushed config fix to backend pool B at 07:35 UTC (added server_name mapping + validated cert chain). Monitoring.
deploy-bot: Rollout note: cert-agent rollout paused in eu-west-1 at 07:28 UTC by @prod_reliability.
network_eng: After backend fix, telemetry shows TLS handshake p99 dropped back to ~140ms within 10 minutes for most POPs. There remains a small tail for sessions that experienced route hairpin earlier.
support_engineer: I've informed customers and provided repro steps to verify: `curl -v --tlsv1.3 https://api.redwood.ai/health -w "%{time_connect}s %{time_appconnect}s" -o /dev/null` should show second value ~0.12s now.
prod_reliability: Followups: 1) Add a canary check verifying SNI/back-end mapping during future cert rotations. 2) Increase route flap alert sensitivity for peering partners. 3) Add automated rollback hook when TLS alert 40 rate > threshold.
infra_lead: Agree. I'll open follow-up tickets for the rollout checklist updates and BGP peer monitoring.
sre_oncall: Closing loop: major mitigation applied (backend fix + paused rollout). Keep this thread open for 24h for any regression. Thanks all :thumbsup:
